paras: Parmigiano-Reggiano comes from a small region in the north of Italy, around Parma. It is made with only three ingredients: milk, salt, and rennet. The producers age each cheese for at least twelve months, and some for more than two years. What makes it unique is the terroir of the region and a tradition that is many centuries old. Today, a geographic indication protects its name, so a cheese from another place cannot use it.

Queijo Canastra comes from the mountains of the Serra da Canastra, in Minas Gerais. Families make it by hand on small farms, with raw milk and a recipe that their grandparents used. Unlike Parmigiano, it is aged for a short time, from a few weeks to a few months, so its flavor is softer. Similar to Parmigiano, it is part of the heritage of its region, and it has a geographic indication too.

For Flavia, the two cheeses tell the same story: a place, its people, and their knowledge. 'Just as Italy has Parmigiano, Brazil has Queijo Canastra,' she says. 'The biodiversity of Brazil gives us hundreds of products like this. If we tell their story well, the world will want to taste them.'

gapfill.text: When you present a product, tell its story in three steps: where it comes from ('It comes from...'), what makes it special ('What makes it unique is...'), and how it compares with something your partner knows ('Similar to... / Unlike...').

listenings.text: Good morning, and welcome to our dairy. My family makes Parmigiano-Reggiano here, near Parma, and we use the same method as my grandfather. The cheese has only three ingredients: milk, salt, and rennet. Every morning, we use the fresh milk from cows in this region. Then, we put each cheese in salt water for about three weeks. After that, we age the cheese for at least twelve months. Some of our cheeses age for two or three years. At the end, an expert checks every cheese. If the cheese is perfect, it gets a special mark. This mark shows that the cheese is authentic. Now, please follow me, and you can taste it.

Welcome back to Travel and Taste. Today, we talk about food and memory. When Brazilians live abroad, what do they miss? Many of them say: Brazilian coffee and cheese bread. For them, these foods are a taste of home. They bring back memories of the family and of the place where they grew up. This is why regional products are so powerful. They are not only food. They are culture. And this is why food fairs are important. At a fair, visitors can taste the product and hear its story. A good story makes people remember the product, and the place it comes from.

extra_audio.text: First, I say the name of the product and where it comes from. Then, I explain how it is traditionally made. Next, I say what makes it unique, like its terroir. After that, I compare it with an Italian product that my partner knows. Finally, I connect the product to the heritage of its region.
